newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SLOW GOING AT CENTURION AS AUSTRALIA DIG IN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SLOW GOING AT CENTURION AS AUSTRALIA DIG IN.

text.p: Australia's batsmen were made to struggle for runs on an attritional first day in the third and final cricket test against South Africa at Centurion Park on Friday.
The normally free-scoring Australians, who hold a winning 2-0 lead in the series, edged their way to 146 for four at tea against some tight South African bowling.
Steve Waugh was 38 not out and Greg Blewett undefeated on 21 at the interval.

After being put in on a well-grassed pitch Australia lost the early wicket of Matthew Hayden, bowled through the gate by recalled fast bowler Brett Schultz for 10, but avoided the dramatic collapse the home side had gambled on.

However, they were made to toil for their runs, adding a modest 80 between lunch and tea as South Africa took the prized wicket of Mark Waugh and chiselled out Mark Taylor, the out-of-form Australian captain.

Resuming after lunch on 62 for two, Waugh, the hero of the second test win in Port Elizabeth earlier in the week, was bowled three overs into the afternoon session for five when Allan Donald beat him for pace.
Taylor had grittily clawed his way to 22 at the interval -- the first time he had reached 20 in 10 test innings -- but a first half-century in 19 innings eluded him once again.
After taking three hours and 17 minutes to reach 38, he aimed a full-blooded drive at a wide, full delivery from Lance Klusener to edge to wicket-keeper Dave Richardson.
In the morning, Schultz, in the side as a replacement for the injured Shaun Pollock, had a hand in both wickets.
After dismissing Hayden in the eighth over of the day, he later produced a fine runnning catch on the fine-leg boundary to punish Matthew Elliott's wayward hook off Donald.
